A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. All 14 pages, including equations, Figures 1–6, Tables 1–5 and Appendices A–E, are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original POPVQA evaluations, activation-patching and attention-knockout experiments, and quantitative and qualitative appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original evaluations and intervention results, including the analyses and examples in Appendices A–C.

M1.justification: The entity-identification and factual-QA procedures, cross patching, forward patching and attention knockouts remain unchanged in Sections 4–6 and Appendix B.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same POPVQA dataset of 15,395 entity-image pairs covering celebrities, landmarks, paintings and brand logos, with unchanged QA and identification scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains LLaVA7B, LM-CLIP, LM-SigLIP, LLaVA34B and Qwen2-VL. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the early/late identification analysis and intervention experiments.

E3.justification: Both retain recognition-conditioned evaluation, per-entity accuracy averaging, 336×336 image preprocessing, the early/late identification split and the same patching and knockout layer settings.

E4.justification: The entity-type breakdowns, within-type and across-type patching, early/late identification analysis, attention-knockout tests and LeBron James/Donald Trump examples are unchanged, including Appendices A–C.

E5.justification: The Wilcoxon signed-rank analysis, plotted uncertainty displays and standard-deviation discussion are retained. Neither version adds or changes seed information, repeated-run counts or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5, Figures 4–6 and Appendix C retain the same values, trends and outputs. For example, Table 1 reports LLaVA7B image accuracy 0.276, text accuracy 0.453 and drop 0.177 in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and notation in Section 2, forward-patching specification in Section 6 and attention-mask specification in Appendix B are unchanged. No formal results or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: POPVQA, the visual-versus-textual knowledge-extraction gap, and evidence that late visual-information processing limits subsequent factual reasoning.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations of middle-layer processing and early identification, alongside the same limitations concerning LLaVA-focused probing, visual confounders and entity/population coverage.

D1.justification: Dataset construction and preprocessing details, code and dataset link targets, and the single A100 80GB or H100 80GB GPU disclosure in Appendix D are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged. MMNeuron retains its title, year, venue and in-text citation; its revised author list is a bibliographic metadata edit.

P1.justification: The MMNeuron reference changes its authors from Jingwei Huo, Yu Yan, Bo Hu, Yuan Yue and Xipeng Hu to Jiahao Huo, Yibo Yan, Boren Hu, Yutao Yue and Xuming Hu. The arXiv version/date stamp also updates; substantive prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised MMNeuron reference wraps differently and slightly changes spacing in the left reference column on PDF page 10. Figures, tables, captions, placements and appendix layouts otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revision is confined to one reference's author metadata, the version stamp and minor reference-page reflow. The main text and appendices retain identical scientific evidence, reasoning, limitations and reproducibility support, leaving overall paper quality materially unchanged.
